Title: On-call agent paged for High/Critical tickets within SLA
StoryText: As an On-call Agent, I want High and Critical severity tickets to page me, so that initial response can begin within the 4 hours documented for High/Critical SLA.
AcceptanceCriteria: High and Critical severity tickets page the on-call agent (per C-003); initial response on High/Critical lands within 4 hours of arrival (per C-007 / NFR-PERF-001).
Notes: Story restates C-003 (paging rule) + C-007 (SLA window) without inventing new conditions; links measurable performance NFR

Title: Engineering escalation includes reproduction steps
StoryText: As a Triage Agent, I want engineering escalations to include reproduction steps, so that engineering does not lose about half a business day per escalation chasing the reporter for context.
AcceptanceCriteria: Engineering escalations carry reproduction steps so the half-business-day escalation slowdown identified in C-006 does not recur.
Notes: Story is a literal reshape of C-006 — same subject (engineering escalation), same condition (missing repro steps), same observable consequence (half-business-day slowdown). No new mechanism invented (e.g., no specific UI control, no enforcement threshold).

Title: Near-duplicate detection at intake prior to agent pickup
StoryText: As a PM, I want near-duplicate tickets detected at intake before agent pickup, so that the approximately 15% of tickets currently detected as duplicates post-claim are caught earlier.
AcceptanceCriteria: Near-duplicate detection runs at intake prior to agent pickup (per C-008 recommendation); the approximately 15% post-claim duplicate rate identified in C-005 decreases.
Notes: Story restates the C-008 recommendation (intake-time duplicate detection) + the C-005 pain-point (approximately 15% post-claim duplicates). INVEST-deferred on Estimable because the duplicate-rate baseline against ticketing-system data is open per A51-001.
